pitches.thesis: Etsy buyers pay $20-60 for automated natal-chart PDFs that Helm & Fortune's existing pipeline produces at near-zero marginal cost with better prose than incumbent sellers.
pitches.customer: Etsy astrology buyers already purchasing $17-59 instant-download natal reports; three real comparables are the sellers of the $59 bundle, the $17-25 one-year forecast, and the 300+ favorite listing observed in the signal.
pitches.why_now: The pipeline (engine -> portraits -> verdict blocks -> prose -> PDF) is already built and running; observed buyer complaints flag incumbent reports as repetitive and padded, which is exactly where a non-template prose pipeline differentiates.
pitches.first_dollar_test: List 3 SKUs on Etsy (single report, bundle, one-year forecast) using existing sample outputs as previews; spend <=$50 on listing fees + minimal promoted listings; measure first sale or 14 days of zero conversions.
pitches.kill_criteria: Zero sales after 30 days with at least 50 listing views, or Etsy fees+ads exceed revenue for two consecutive months.
pitches.why_not_already_done: Most Etsy sellers run one-shot software templates; a genuinely varied multi-pass prose pipeline with an astrology practitioner's QA is rarer than the listings suggest.
pitches.biggest_unknown: Whether a new Etsy shop with no reviews can get any impressions at all in a saturated, fee-heavy search category (per the signal's own caution).

pitches.thesis: Hudson Valley small contractors pay a flat January-season fee to have their 1099 payouts reconciled and forms prepared via SplitRail rails the operator already built.
pitches.customer: Small GCs and subs in the Saugerties-Rhinebeck-Kingston corridor paying 2-10 1099 workers; three nameable prospects come directly from the operator's existing trade network.
pitches.price: $150 per contractor for a January 1099 season package
pitches.why_now: The 1099-NEC threshold moved $600 -> $2,000 for 2026; contractors who paid subs in that band learn about the change from bookkeepers in January and need their records reconciled against it.
pitches.first_dollar_test: Call/message 10 contractors from the trade network offering the January package; pre-sell 2 at $150 payable now or at delivery. No software changes required beyond what SplitRail already does.
pitches.kill_criteria: Fewer than 2 paid commitments after 10 direct asks, or all prospects say their bookkeeper already handles it cheaply.
pitches.why_not_already_done: National SaaS targets general contractors at scale; nobody is selling a hands-on, local, season-priced service to 2-10 sub shops through warm relationships.
pitches.biggest_unknown: Whether the threshold change creates or reduces pain (it raises the bar, so it may mean fewer forms and less urgency).

pitches.thesis: Helm & Fortune's existing subscribers pay a $17-25 add-on for a software-generated one-year forecast PDF, sold into an audience the operator already owns.
pitches.customer: Current Helm & Fortune paying subscribers on the lunation/daily tiers; three real ones are existing subscribers the operator can email this week.
pitches.why_now: Etsy comparables prove $17-25 one-year forecast PDFs sell; the operator already has both the paying audience and the generation pipeline, so this avoids the Etsy cold-start problem entirely.
pitches.first_dollar_test: Email the existing subscriber list a one-time offer for the one-year forecast PDF at $19; generate manually from the pipeline on order. Goal: 3 sales.
pitches.kill_criteria: Zero sales from the full subscriber list after one offer email and one reminder, or refund/complaint rate above 15%.
pitches.why_not_already_done: Most practitioners hand-write forecasts; combining an automated pipeline with an existing paying audience is an operator-specific edge, not a generic one.
pitches.biggest_unknown: Subscriber list size and open rates - if the list is tiny, the ceiling is low even at high conversion.

pitches.thesis: KalshiML's weather forecasting/calibration machinery is applied to Polymarket's 126-164 daily temperature markets, capturing edge on contracts the Kalshi-only stack already knows how to price.
pitches.customer: Self-directed trading (the 'customer' is the market); no named external customer needed for first dollar.
pitches.why_now: Polymarket runs a large book of daily-temp markets in the same contract shape KML already models; the stack is currently paper-only on Kalshi, and a second venue doubles the surface for the same research.
pitches.first_dollar_test: Add one Polymarket city already modeled (or closest available), paper-trade for 7 days logging predicted edge vs resolution; first real dollar only if paper shows positive calibrated edge.
pitches.kill_criteria: Paper P&L negative or calibration no better than market-implied after 20 resolved markets, or resolution-source mismatch makes edge untradeable.
pitches.why_not_already_done: Most weather-market traders focus on one venue; running calibrated multi-venue weather models with an existing gating engine is uncommon at this scale.
pitches.biggest_unknown: The heavily traded cities (Hong Kong, London, Shanghai) are outside KML's current model coverage, Open-Meteo quota is binding, and settlement mechanics differ from Kalshi.

pitches.thesis: Contractors and tradespeople in the operator's network pay for fast, practical horary readings (lost tools, bid timing, job questions) delivered as short PDFs from the existing pipeline.
pitches.customer: Tradespeople and small business owners already in the operator's Hudson Valley network who are curious-but-not-clients; three nameable prospects exist in the network today.
pitches.why_now: Etsy proves automated astrology PDFs sell at $17-59; a horary product sold person-to-person through the trade network sidesteps marketplace saturation and tests whether the pipeline has offline demand.
pitches.first_dollar_test: Offer horary readings to 5 warm contacts at $35 each, fulfill via pipeline with practitioner review; one week, zero build.
pitches.kill_criteria: Zero paid questions from 5 warm offers, or all buyers treat it as a one-off joke gift with no repeat interest.
pitches.why_not_already_done: Astrology is rarely sold through blue-collar warm networks at practical price points; the channel itself is the differentiator.
pitches.biggest_unknown: Whether this audience pays at all - the demand signal is from Etsy buyers, a very different population, so this may be demand transference error.

pitches.thesis: SplitRail's multi-tenant payout machinery is offered as a white-label batch-payout service to one adjacent local business (e.g., a cleaning or landscaping company paying a crew), with no new platform build.
pitches.customer: Owner-operated local service businesses paying 3-15 1099 workers manually; three nameable candidates reachable through the trade network within one referral.
pitches.price: $25/mo flat for batch payouts + season-end records
pitches.why_now: Vendor literature confirms missed deadlines and TIN errors as persistent pains, and the 2026 threshold change puts payout records on bookkeepers' radar this January; the rails are already built and multi-tenant.
pitches.first_dollar_test: Pitch 3 adjacent-business owners directly; offer to run their next payout batch manually through SplitRail for $25. One paid batch = validated.
pitches.kill_criteria: Zero paid batches after 3 direct pitches, or onboarding friction requires >5 hours of manual work per client per month.
pitches.why_not_already_done: Incumbent tools (Routable et al.) sell to larger firms with sales teams; a $25/mo local service sold warm is below their floor.
pitches.biggest_unknown: The demand evidence is competitor marketing, not measured demand - small operators may be content with Venmo + spreadsheets despite the pain.
